tooling.message:
feat(rules): give the rules of the plan workflow and the tooling the scope tooling

## Intent

The catalog takes apps however they are built. Ten rules presuppose the plan workflow or the tooling's checks, yet had scope listing and applied to every app, so a freely built app would fail for a missing plan file. Hold such an app to the listing rules alone.

## Key changes

- plan-file, explore-before-code, stop-at-checkpoints, few-turns-after-plan, retrospective-filled, app-content-guide, app-content-matches, checks-pass, fix-from-message and suppression-reason move from scope listing to the new scope tooling.
- They apply to an app built with the tooling, at listing too. The marker is the one every generated app already has: @lernapps/tooling in the package.json's dependencies or devDependencies.
- `npm run rules -- --app <dir>` lists the rules in scope for one app. The review judges those alone; the rubric judges plan-file for an app built with the tooling that has no plan.
- Ids, texts and severities stay as they were.

## Dependencies and side effects

- lernapps/apps c48de7a (same intent) gives the review agent only the rules in scope.

feat(review): give the review agent only the rules in scope for the app

## Intent

A freely built app should not be judged by plan-file, retrospective-filled or the other rules of the plan workflow.

## Key changes

- The review's rules.yaml comes from `npm run --silent rules -- --app <app>` of lernapps/tooling: the listing rules, the rules of scope tooling only when the app's package.json lists @lernapps/tooling, and the rules of its plan's archetype.

## Dependencies and side effects

- Needs lernapps/tooling c6e40d2 (same intent) on main.
